q: A 36-year-old woman (G4 P2103) at 23 weeks of gestation presents with a primary attack of herpes simplex virus infection. Acyclovir is given orally for 10 days. Which of the following is the rationale for acyclovir treatment?
o: Decrease the herpes simplex virus infection
Decrease viral shedding and the duration of the current infection
k: Antivirals in HSV control replication (shedding and symptoms); they never eradicate latent virus.
r: Neonatal herpes is a birth canal infection, so any option about the placenta is a distractor.
n: مكرر (OCT-9032) وجوابه هناك: Decrease viral shedding and current infection dura. جواب القناة (علامة الاستفتاء)، غير مؤكد.

q: A patient is admitted following a motor vehicle accident. Initially stable, a head CT showed a small epidural hematoma with no midline shift. Six hours later, the patient becomes drowsy and develops a dilated pupil. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
A 7-year-old child presents for evaluation of short stature. Physical examination and growth velocity are normal, but bone age is delayed. What is the most appropriate management?
o: Reassure that the child will reach adult height
k: Short stature fork: Familial: normal bone age, normal velocity, short parents, short but on target final height; Constitutional: delayed bone age, normal velocity, late puberty in family, normal final height, reassure; Pathological: delayed bone age, slow velocity, treat cause (± growth hormone if G
r: Delayed bone age alone is not pathological; delayed bone age plus slow velocity is.
n: مكرر (SWR-0148) وجوابه هناك: reassure it will catch the adult height. جواب القناة (علامة الاستفتاء)، غير مؤكد.

q: An eight-month-old infant is brought to the clinic with a history of multiple pyogenic infections caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, recurrent otitis media, and pneumonia. The mother also reports that the infant has chronic diarrhea. Which of the following investigations is required to reach the diagnosis?
k: Match the infection pattern to the immune arm: Encapsulated bacteria, sinopulmonary infections, onset after 6 months, Giardia: B-cell/antibody defect, test immunoglobulins.; Viral, fungal, opportunistic infections, failure to thrive from early infancy: T-cell or combined defect (SCID), test lymphocy
r: Infections that start only after 6 months of age point to antibody deficiency, because maternal IgG protected the first months.
n: مكرر (SWR-0220) وجوابه هناك: Immunoglobulin levels. جواب القناة (علامة الاستفتاء)، غير مؤكد.
kw: multiple pyogenic infections with Streptococcus pneumoniae

A couple presents to an infertility clinic complaining of inability to conceive. The husband's semen count is normal. A hysterosalpingogram reveals bilateral blocked tubes. What is the next step in management?
k: Tubal factor ladder: HSG is the initial test of tubal patency; Abnormal HSG: confirm with diagnostic laparoscopy and dye test; Confirmed unilateral block: ovulation induction (clomiphene)
r: HSG only plus laparoscopy offered = laparoscopy; laparoscopy not offered or already done = IVF.
n: مكرر (OCT-5936) وجوابه هناك: In vitro fertilization. جواب القناة (علامة الاستفتاء)، غير مؤكد.
